mcqs.question: What is a primary method used by international tribunals and arbiters to establish the meaning in context of a treaty?
options: Reviewing only the final, signed treaty itself
Reviewing only the preparatory work from the negotiation and drafting of the treaty
Reviewing both the preparatory work and the final, signed treaty
mcqs.explanation: The text states that international tribunals and arbiters may review both the preparatory work from the negotiation and drafting of the treaty as well as the final, signed treaty itself.
mcqs.source_text: International tribunals and arbiters are often called upon to resolve substantial disputes over treaty interpretations. To establish the meaning in context, these judicial bodies may review the preparatory work from the negotiation and drafting of the treaty as well as the final, signed treaty itself.

mcqs.question: Who established a permanent Qing dynasty garrison in Tibet?
mcqs.explanation: The text states that during the reign of the Qianlong Emperor (r. 1735-1796), a permanent Qing dynasty garrison was established in Tibet.
mcqs.source_text: When the Dzungar Mongols attempted to spread their territory from what is now Xinjiang into Tibet, the Kangxi Emperor (r. 1661–1722) responded to Tibetan pleas for aid with his own expedition to Tibet, occupying Lhasa in 1720. By 1751, during the reign of the Qianlong Emperor (r. 1735–1796), a protectorate and permanent Qing dynasty garrison was established in Tibet. As of 1751, Albert Kolb writes that "Chinese claims to suzerainty over Tibet date from this time."
